title: Neuromorphic Continuity vs State Saving
summary: How does ‘memory’ works in neuromorphic machines?
content_html:
Neuromorphic Continuity vs State Saving

How does ‘memory’ works in neuromorphic machines?

You don’t need to run indefinitely to study “memory”.** Neuromorphic machines support saving their structural (long‑term) state — synaptic weights, delays, routing tables, model parameters — and restoring it later. What is lost on pause is the dynamic (short‑term) state — ongoing spike trains, membrane voltages, and transient conductances. In other words, you can persist the wiring/knowledge, but not the current thought.

Question Answer
Do these machines need to run forever to keep memory? No.
Persisted weights/config suffice for long‑term memory.
Can I snapshot and resume mid‑thought? Not exactly.
You’ll lose transient voltages and in‑flight spikes.
Can I replicate behavior after restore? Yes,
by restoring config and replaying inputs; trajectories may differ but function can match.

Two Layers of Memory

Layer Analogy Persists Across Stop/Start? How It’s Handled
Structural (long‑term) Synaptic weights, delays, rules Yes Serialize parameters/config; reload later
Dynamic (short‑term) Active spikes, membrane voltages No Exists only while running; re‑emerges from inputs

Experiment Patterns

  • Long experiments with learning: run continuously; periodically checkpoint weights to disk.
  • Stop‑and‑study: run to a target condition; dump configuration + recorded data; reload to replicate.
  • Reconstruction: after restore, provide identical inputs/stimuli to recreate population dynamics statistically.

Implications for “Memory” Research

  • Working memory phenomena (persistent activity, oscillations) require continuous operation during observation.
  • Long‑term memory (learned connectivity) survives power cycles via serialization.
  • Causality: when resuming, the exact micro‑timing of spikes will differ; what matters is reproducible function, not bit‑identical trajectories.
